title: Coco Gauff Wins Big Before US Open!
summary:
Tennis star Coco Gauff is on fire! She just won the Cincinnati Open, beating her friend and fellow American Jessica Pegula in the final. The score was 6-2, 6-4, and it only took 1 hour and 14 minutes. That's super fast!

This is Coco's first title of 2026, and it's a big one. She's only the third woman to win this tournament twice, joining legends Serena Williams and Victoria Azarenka. Pretty cool, right?

But here's the exciting part: the last time Coco won in Cincinnati was in 2023, and just three weeks later, she won her first Grand Slam title at the US Open! So fans are hoping history repeats itself. The US Open starts on August 30, and Coco is one of the favorites to win.

Coco said she's feeling confident: "I think with each match, I was feeling more and more confident in trusting the work that I put in and the practice." She only lost one set the whole tournament. That's amazing!

There's also a French player named Arthur Fils who won the men's title in Cincinnati. He's 22 years old and had a back injury that kept him out for nine months. He came back in February and has now won two titles. He said, "Wow, that feels good. That feels good." He's now ranked 11th in the world, his best ever.

So get ready for the US Open—it's going to be exciting!
why_it_matters: Coco's story shows that hard work and believing in yourself can help you do amazing things, whether in sports or in school.

background_read: The Cincinnati Open is an important tennis tournament that happens every summer before the US Open (one of the four biggest tennis tournaments in the world).

Coco Gauff (an American tennis star) now joins Serena Williams (one of the greatest tennis players ever) and Victoria Azarenka (a former champion from Belarus) as the only women to win Cincinnati twice.
Winning a warm-up tournament is not a guarantee, but it can give players extra confidence for the Grand Slam ahead.
